resposta:
Based on my research, here is a comprehensive report on all the Nightlord bosses in Elden Ring: Nightreign and their unique first-time drop relics.

# **Elden Ring: Nightreign - Complete Nightlord Report**

## **Overview**
Nightreign features 8 primary Nightlord bosses (plus 2 DLC-exclusive ones) that players face at the end of each expedition's third night. Each Nightlord has unique mechanics, weaknesses, and rewards. Defeating them for the first time unlocks new expeditions and grants exclusive relics.

---

## **Primary Nightlords (Base Game)**

### **1. Gladius, Beast of Night (Tricephalos)**
- **Expedition:** Tricephalos
- **Appearance:** Three-headed wolf with a chained sword
- **Weakness:** Holy Damage
- **First-Time Drops:**
  - **Relic:** Night of the Beast (Stamina recovery +1 per attack; starting armament deals fire damage)
  - **Relic:** Old Pocketwatch (FP restoration on successive attacks; Dexterity +3)
  - **Unique Item:** Primordial Nightlord's Rune (upon defeating Everdark Sovereign version)

### **2. Adel, Baron of Night (Gaping Jaw)**
- **Expedition:** Gaping Jaw
- **Appearance:** Massive black dragon with horizontal jaw
- **Weakness:** Poison
- **First-Time Drops:**
  - **Relic:** Night of the Baron (unique effects)
  - **Relic:** Dark Night of the Baron (available after Everdark Sovereign victory)

### **3. Gnoster, Wisdom of Night (Sentient Pest)**
- **Expedition:** Sentient Pest
- **Appearance:** Duo of a great white moth (Gnoster) and mole cricket-like insect (Faurtis Stoneshield)
- **Weakness:** Fire Damage
- **First-Time Drops:**
  - **Relic:** Night of the Wise (unique effects)
  - **Relic:** Dark Night of the Wise (available after Everdark Sovereign victory)

### **4. Maris, Fathom of Night (Augur)**
- **Expedition:** Augur
- **Appearance:** Aquatic squid-like entity
- **Weakness:** Lightning Damage
- **First-Time Drops:**
  - **Relic:** Night of the Fathom (unique effects)
  - **Relic:** Dark Night of the Fathom (available after Everdark Sovereign victory)
  - **Special Drop:** Legendary Storm Ruler weapon (Everdark Sovereign Phase 1)

### **5. Libra, Creature of Night (Equilibrious Beast)**
- **Expedition:** Equilibrious Beast
- **Appearance:** Goat-headed humanoid using alchemy
- **Weakness:** Madness (also weak to Fire, Slash, Holy)
- **First-Time Drops:**
  - **Relic:** Night of the Demon (unique effects)
  - **Relic:** Dark Night of the Demon (available after Everdark Sovereign victory)

### **6. Fulghor, Champion of Nightglow (Darkdrift Knight)**
- **Expedition:** Darkdrift Knight
- **Appearance:** One-armed masked centaur with massive sword
- **Weakness:** Lightning Damage
- **First-Time Drops:**
  - **Relic:** Night of the Champion (unique effects)
  - **Relic:** Dark Night of the Champion (available after Everdark Sovereign victory)

### **7. Caligo, Miasma of Night (Fissure in the Fog)**
- **Expedition:** Fissure in the Fog
- **Appearance:** Dragon with icy powers resembling an Everlasting Dragon
- **Weakness:** Fire Damage
- **First-Time Drops:**
  - **Relic:** Night of the Miasma (unique effects)
  - **Relic:** Dark Night of the Miasma (available after Everdark Sovereign victory)

### **8. Heolstor the Nightlord (Night Aspect)**
- **Expedition:** Night Aspect
- **Appearance:** Primordial figure representing the origin of Night itself
- **Weakness:** Holy Damage
- **First-Time Drops:**
  - **Relic:** Night of the Lord (unique effects)
  - **Relic:** Primordial Nightlord's Rune (special item)
  - **Note:** Can perform Scarlet Rot-infused attacks if Forsaken Hollows DLC is owned

---

## **DLC Exclusive Nightlords (The Forsaken Hollows)**

### **9. Traitorous Straghess (Dreglord)**
- **Expedition:** Dreglord
- **Appearance:** Corpse fiend made of countless bodies and discarded detritus
- **Weakness:** None obvious (no special-effect weakness)
- **First-Time Drops:**
  - **Relic:** The Night of Dregs (unique effects)

### **10. Weapon-Bequeathed Harmonia (Balancers)**
- **Expedition:** Balancers
- **Appearance:** Seven Valkyries clad in white armor wielding heroic weapons
- **Weakness:** Sleep (extremely vulnerable)
- **First-Time Drops:**
  - **Relic:** The Will of the Balancers (unique effects)

---

## **Key Notes**

1. **Everdark Sovereign Variants:** All Nightlords have harder "Everdark Sovereign" versions available weekly. Defeating these for the first time unlocks "Dark [Nightlord Name]" relics from the Collector Signboard.

2. **Remembrance Quests:** Some Nightlords are required for specific Nightfarer remembrance quests (e.g., Gladius or Fulghor for Revenant's quest).

3. **Randomized Rewards:** While the main relics are guaranteed, additional random relics may drop alongside the standard rewards.

4. **Unlock Requirements:** To unlock DLC Nightlords, players must defeat at least two Nightlords (including Gladius) and ensure both Scholar and Undertaker Nightfarers are playable.

5. **No Repeatable Victories:** Unlike traditional FromSoftware games, Nightlord victories cannot be reattempted quickly, making first-time drops particularly valuable.

This report covers all current Nightlord content as of the latest game updates through mid-2026.

**Bosses** are powerful [enemies](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightreign_Enemies "Nightreign Enemies") that can be encountered in *[Elden Ring Nightreign](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Elden_Ring_Nightreign "Elden Ring Nightreign")*.

## Overview[]

Boss encounters in [Limveld](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Limveld "Limveld") are randomized at the start of each [Expedition](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Expeditions "Expeditions"). Minor bosses roam the region during the day, while a powerful boss appears at the end of each night. Surviving two in-game nights leads to a climactic battle against one of eight final [Nightlord bosses](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightlords "Nightlords").

## Nightlords[]

Nightlords are fought on the third night. Unlike other encounters, the final boss is not randomized; instead, they are selected between rounds by interacting with the [Table of Lost Grace](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Table_of_Lost_Grace "Table of Lost Grace") at the [Roundtable Hold](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Roundtable_Hold_(Nightreign) "Roundtable Hold (Nightreign)").[[1]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightreign_Bosses#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightreign_Bosses#cite_note-Famitsu-2)[[3]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightreign_Bosses#cite_note-IGN3-3)

## Nightlord Weaknesses[]

Each Nightlord has a scripted weakness to a particular source of damage. For example, dealing even a small amount of [Lightning damage](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Lightning_damage "Lightning damage") to [Maris, Fathom of Night](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Maris,_Fathom_of_Night "Maris, Fathom of Night") as it channels its global [Sleep](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sleep "Sleep") spell is enough to break its [stance](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Stance "Stance") and cancel the attack. The [damage negation](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Damage_Negation "Damage Negation") and [status resistances](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Resistance "Resistance") for each Nightlord boss are listed in the table below. A **positive** value indicates reduced negation (more damage taken), while a **negative** value indicates increased damage negation (less damage taken). For [Resistances](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Resistance "Resistance"), lower values indicate a vulnerability (faster buildup), while higher values require more buildup to inflict the [Status Ailment](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Status_Effects "Status Effects"). These weaknesses still apply if the boss is fought on Day 1 or Day 2.

- [Damage Types](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Damage_Types "Damage Types")
  - +0% indicates that a boss is neutral to that damage type.
  - A positive value (+%) indicates bonus damage.
  - A negative value (-% -% -%) indicates that a boss is resistant to the damage type.

- [Resistances](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Resistances "Resistances")
  - A lower value indicates faster procs of the applicable status effect.
  - The **🛇** symbol denotes full immunity to the status effect.

## Everdark Sovereigns[]

[Everdark Sovereigns](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Everdark_Sovereigns "Everdark Sovereigns") are challenging versions of the standard [Expeditions](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Expeditions "Expeditions"), available for a limited time on a weekly rotation. The Everdark Sovereigns in active weekly rotation are [Tricephalos](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Tricephalos "Tricephalos"), [Gaping Jaw](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Gaping_Jaw "Gaping Jaw"), [Sentient Pest](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sentient_Pest "Sentient Pest"), [Augur](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Augur "Augur"), [Equilibrious Beast](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Equilibrious_Beast "Equilibrious Beast"), [Darkdrift Knight](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Darkdrift_Knight "Darkdrift Knight"), and [Fissure in the Fog](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Fissure_in_the_Fog "Fissure in the Fog"). Additional Everdark Sovereign Expeditions are scheduled to appear in future [updates](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightreign_Updates "Nightreign Updates"). This feature is not available in offline mode.

Players can only challenge an Everdark Sovereign after defeating its standard [Nightlord](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightlords "Nightlords") form. The Nightlord **bosses** of Everdark Sovereign missions are significantly more difficult, featuring upgraded strength and new movesets. They start at Phase 2 and advance to an empowered Phase 3. Defeating an Everdark Sovereign grants [![Sovereign Sigil](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/ERN_Icon_Menu_Sovereign_Sigil.png)](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sovereign_Sigil "Sovereign Sigil") [Sovereign Sigils](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sovereign_Sigil "Sovereign Sigil"), with a bonus for first-time victories. Sigils can be exchanged for exclusive [Relics](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Relics "Relics") and other rare items at the [Collector Signboard](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Collector_Signboard "Collector Signboard").

## *The Forsaken Hollows* Bosses[]

The *[Elden Ring Nightreign: The Forsaken Hollows](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Elden_Ring_Nightreign:_The_Forsaken_Hollows "Elden Ring Nightreign: The Forsaken Hollows")* DLC adds the following boss encounters:

- [Ancestral Follower Warriors](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Ancestral_Follower_Warriors "Ancestral Follower Warriors") (can be found in Lightning forges)
- [Ancestor Spirit](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Ancestor_Spirit "Ancestor Spirit")
- [Balancers](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Balancers "Balancers") (appear during the Balancers Raid)
- [Banished Knights](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Banished_Knights "Banished Knights")
- [Blackflame Monks](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Blackflame_Monks "Blackflame Monks") (can be found in Fire forges)
- [Bloodbane Giant Crows](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Bloodbane_Giant_Crows "Bloodbane Giant Crows")
- [Bloodhound Knight](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Bloodhound_Knight "Bloodhound Knight")
- [Bloodhound Knights](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Bloodhound_Knights "Bloodhound Knights")
- [Chief Bloodfiend](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Chief_Bloodfiend "Chief Bloodfiend")

## Cataclysm Condemned[]

Condemned [Nightfarers](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightfarers "Nightfarers") invade at locations affected by Cataclysms. Although they are not marked as bosses, they drop [Dormant Powers](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Dormant_Power "Dormant Power") upon defeat. The loot is always a rare upgraded version of that class's starting weapon. The following Condemned may appear:

- Night Assassin ([Ironeye](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Ironeye "Ironeye"))
- Night Deceiver ([Scholar](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Scholar "Scholar"))
- Night Executor ([Executor](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Executor "Executor"))
- Night Fallen ([Guardian](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Guardian_(hero) "Guardian (hero)"))
- Night Hunter ([Wylder](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Wylder "Wylder"))

## Notes[]

- Bosses are promoted or simply get stronger on day two.
- Bosses do not regenerate [health](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/HP "HP") over time or between days.
- Defeating a boss creates a [Site of Grace](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Sites_of_Grace "Sites of Grace") and a blue, purple, or gold [Dormant Power](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Dormant_Power "Dormant Power"). Interacting with the object opens a menu with two to three reward choices. [Nightfarers](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightfarers "Nightfarers") may obtain boss loot even if they were too far away to earn [runes](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Runes "Runes"). The object will not vanish or expire between days.
  - They can drop [Armaments](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightreign_Armaments "Nightreign Armaments"), [Smithing Stones](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Smithing_Stones "Smithing Stones"), or a passive [boon](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightreign_Effects#Dormant_Powers "Nightreign Effects") that is bound to the character for the remainder of the Expedition.
- [Evergaols](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Evergaols "Evergaols") contain bosses, but must be unlocked with a [Stonesword Key](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Stonesword_Key "Stonesword Key").
- [Version 1.01](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightreign_Updates "Nightreign Updates"): the [Runebear](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Runebear "Runebear") duo boss is currently bugged on PC. Only one bear has the boss HP bar but both bears drop boss loot.[verified]

## Trivia[]

- Eight all-new Nightlord bosses were crafted for *Nightreign*.
- Many bosses first appeared in [*Dark Souls*](https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/Dark_Souls "w:c:darksouls:Dark Souls"), [*Dark Souls II*](https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/Dark_Souls_II "w:c:darksouls:Dark Souls II"), [*Dark Souls III*](https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/Dark_Souls_III "w:c:darksouls:Dark Souls III"), and *[Elden Ring](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Elden_Ring_(game) "Elden Ring (game)")*.
  - With the release of Forsaken Hollows, Dark Souls 2 has the least amount of returning bosses at only 2, while Dark Souls 1 and 3 got 3.
- Some returning *Elden Ring* bosses were renamed to be more generic. Many use "new" moves that were originally [cut content](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Unused_Content "Unused Content").
  - A few of the [Demigods](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Demigods "Demigods") make an appearance. [Morgott, the Omen King](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Morgott,_the_Omen_King "Morgott, the Omen King") returns with an updated moveset, Alongside [Godrick the Grafted](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Godrick_the_Grafted "Godrick the Grafted").
- Unlike previous [FromSoftware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FromSoftware "wp:FromSoftware") titles, bosses in *Nightreign* cannot be reattempted in quick succession.[[2]](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightreign_Bosses#cite_note-Famitsu-2)
- The Fire Monk boss was mislabeled as "Fire Prelate" during the [Nightreign Network Test](https://eldenring.fandom.com/wiki/Nightreign_Network_Test "Nightreign Network Test").

### Inside Magic: The Gathering SDCC 2026 | Collector's Quest

Step inside the Hasbro booth at San Diego Comic-Con as we sit down with Mark Rosewater, Head Designer for Magic: The Gathering, to discuss the highly anticipated Marvel collaboration!

We get an inside look at the creative brainstorming process behind bringing Earth's Mightiest Heroes to the tabletop—including how a giant whiteboard helped shape the set, the inspiration behind an unexpected "deep cut" character choice, and how the design team created brand-new gameplay mechanics for iconic artifacts like Thor's hammer, Mjölnir. We also explore how famous comic book locations were selected for land cards before wrapping things up by opening a fresh booster pack right on the show floor to see what cards we pull!

[![](https://cdn.jwplayer.com/v2/media/x49BfqzK/poster.jpg?width=720)](https://cdn.jwplayer.com/videos/x49BfqzK-cSpmBcaY.mp4)

**Bosses** in **[Nightreign](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Elden_Ring_Nightreign_Wiki "Elden Ring Nightreign Wiki")** are powerful enemies that bring intense challenges throughout the game. These encounters can show up both out in the overworld and within more traditional points of interest. Some bosses are required to progress through the game, while many others are entirely optional. Every boss comes with its own unique set of attacks and gear, along with specific weaknesses and resistances to different damage types and playstyles. While some of the underlying mechanics carry over from Elden Ring, the bosses in Nightreign are deadlier overall, since they bring extra moves and new tactics into combat. On top of the challenge, players still walk away with unique rewards once a boss is successfully defeated. This page covers all the known bosses currently found in **Elden Ring Nightreign**.

s darkness falls over Limveld, the [Night's Tide](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Night%27s_Tide "Night's Tide") begins creeping across the field, shrinking the space players have to move around in. Once night fully sets in, the group is pushed toward a confrontation that can't be avoided. A brutal battle follows as a number of powerful enemies converge on the player. Allies may end up falling to these enemies' devastating attacks, but that doesn't mean the fight is over. Critically injured allies can be brought back into the fight by attacking them with [Skills](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Skills "Skills") and [Weapons](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Weapons "Weapons"). They can also be rescued from a distance using tools such as bows or magic. These battles are demanding, but the message is clear: don't give up. Players are meant to draw on everything they've gathered throughout Limveld in order to survive and come out on top.

## Bosses Guide in Elden Ring Nightreign

### Elden Ring Nightreign Table of Contents

- [Nightreign Bosses: Guides](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Bosses#guide)
- [Nightrein Bosses: Complete List](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Bosses#list)

### Types of Bosses in Elden Ring Nightreign

- **Nightlords** serve as the primary bosses of Elden Ring Nightreign. Before matchmaking begins, players can select a targeted Nightlord at the [Roundtable Hold](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Roundtable_Hold "Roundtable Hold"). After the Night Boss is defeated on Day 2, players are teleported to a realm called the "Spirit Shelter," where they can purchase items to prepare for the Nightlord waiting behind a large stone door. In total, there are 8 Nightlords in Elden Ring Nightreign.
- **Night Bosses** show up at the end of every day, and which one appears depends on the specific day and expedition. As the Ring of Blue Flames closes in, the area available for exploration gradually shrinks. Once the Ring reaches its appropriate size, the Night Boss is summoned. **These bosses are non-optional and must be defeated to progress onto the next day.**
- **Evergaol Bosses** are found inside Evergaols, which can only be opened using Stonesword Keys. The later in the run a gaol is opened, the more powerful its boss tends to be.
- **Field Bosses appear** in open areas scattered across Limveld. While the same locations will always contain a boss across every expedition, the specific boss that shows up there can vary. The most dangerous Field Bosses are marked on the map with a [![formidable enemy](https://static0.fextralifeimages.com/file/eldenringnightreign/thumb/0/05/Formidable-enemy.png/25px-Formidable-enemy.png)](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/File:Formidable-enemy.png) icon right at the start of Day 2.
- **Location Bosses** can be found within points of interest that are marked on the map, like [Ruins](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Ruins "Ruins") and [Tunnels](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Tunnel_Entrance "Tunnel Entrance").
- **Remembrance Bosses** are exclusive bosses that are only encountered when players relive a Nightfarer's [Remembrance Quest](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Remembrance_Quests "Remembrance Quests"). These bosses require players to progress a Nightfarer's quest to fight them. Some are fought in the [Roundtable Hold](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Roundtable_Hold "Roundtable Hold") and some in [Limveld](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Limveld "Limveld"). Defeating Remembrance Bosses also rewards players with unique [Key Items](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Key_Items "Key Items") that are mainly used for progressing remembrance quests.
- **Shifting Earth Bosses** always appear when particular [Shifting Earth](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Shifting_Earth "Shifting Earth") maps are active, in or around the part of the map changed by the Shifting Earth. They're more likely to drop rewards that match the [affinity](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Weapon_Reward "Weapon Reward") of the current Shifting Earth.
- **Event Bosses** pop up randomly during expeditions, usually without any warning beforehand. They offer powerful, unique rewards to players who manage to defeat them, but failing the challenge can come with a curse instead.

**The bosses** found in **Nightreign** draw from a range of other FromSoftware titles, including Dark Souls, Dark Souls II, Dark Souls III, and Elden Ring. One notable difference from those other games is that dying during a boss fight in Nightreign doesn't reset your progress right away. Instead, a teammate can revive you so the fight can continue. It's only when every member of the party has been downed that the whole group gets teleported to a Respawn area.

### How to Unlock New Bosses in Elden Ring Nightreign

Players must meet the following conditions to unlock the new bosses in Nightreign's Forsaken Hollows:

- Defeated at least two Nightlords, which includes [Gladius Beast of Night](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Gladius_Beast_of_Night "Gladius Beast of Night") ([Tricephalos](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Tricephalos "Tricephalos")) and one other Nightlord.
- Ensure that both new [Nightfarers](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Nightfarers_(classes) "Nightfarers (classes)"), [Scholar](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Scholar "Scholar") and [Undertaker](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Undertaker "Undertaker"), are unlocked and playable.

[![unlock bosses dlc elden ring nightreign wiki guide 400px](https://static0.fextralifeimages.com/file/eldenringnightreign/2/22/Unlock-bosses-dlc-elden-ring-nightreign-wiki-guide-400px.png)](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/File:Unlock-bosses-dlc-elden-ring-nightreign-wiki-guide-720px.png "File:Unlock-bosses-dlc-elden-ring-nightreign-wiki-guide-720px.png")

Once both of these conditions are met, players should head back to the chapel that opens up behind the [Small Jar Bazaar](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Small_Jar_Bazaar "Small Jar Bazaar") at the [Roundtable Hold](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Roundtable_Hold "Roundtable Hold"). It's also worth noting that in post-release patches, the Shifting Earth, Raid Events, and bases introduced through the Forsaken Hollows DLC will begin appearing in [Deep of Night](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Deep_of_Night "Deep of Night"), even during expeditions run in the base game.

**NOTE**: One thing to keep in mind: for this DLC-exclusive content to actually show up in Deep of Night, you'll need to be matched with three players who all own the DLC.

### Night Bosses in ER Nightreign

The Nightlords stand as the ultimate threat, waiting for players on the third day in limbo. The Nightfarers are the only warriors left who have a chance at stopping them and saving the land from total destruction.

Taking on a Nightlord is a different kind of challenge altogether, since these beings boast overwhelming attack power and toughness that surpasses anything players will have faced up to that point. Even so, there are ways to push back against this threat.

By carefully making their way through limbo, picking up more powerful tools and weapons with attributes that work well against each specific Nightlord, uncovering relics along the way, and growing sharper as a fighter through experience and observation, players can put victory against the Nightlord within reach.

The negation numbers are the % of your damage that gets blocked. For example, if a negation is 60, 40% of that damage by that type will go through and 60% will be negated. Bigger number = less damage. A negation of 100 means no damage goes through, and a negation of -100 mean the enemy takes 2x damage from that source. 0 means damage goes pretty much as is.

The resistance numbers are the buildup amount to trigger it. For example, if a resistance is 100 you must deal 100 points of the given buildup to trigger it. Note that these go down over time, and increase each time the effect procs. The values after the "/"s indicate the increased resistances after each successive proc.

**Gladius Beast of Night**, also known as **Tricephalos,** is a **[Nightlord](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Bosses "Bosses")** in **[Nightreign](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Elden_Ring_Nightreign_Wiki "Elden Ring Nightreign Wiki").** This is the first Nightlord that players typically encounter. It takes the form of a three-headed wolf with the unique ability to split itself into three separate wolves. As with other Nightlords, this is a challenging Night Boss faced on the third and final day, bringing its own distinct move set, weaknesses, resistances, skills, and abilities to the encounter. Coordinated attacks from the whole group are necessary to bring it down and come out victorious. Gladius Beast of Night is specifically the Nightlord encountered during the Tricephalos expedition.

- [Click here for the Everdark Sovereign variant of Gladius Beast of Night](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Gladius_Beast_of_Night_Everdark_Sovereign_(tricephalos) "Gladius Beast of Night Everdark Sovereign (tricephalos)")

> A many-legged beast appearing from shadow, carrying on its back a chain-link sword used to hunt its prey. Between the fangs of its many heads flicker overwhelming flames. When assailed by multiple shadows, only sacred light can hinder the hunt.

### Elden Ring Gladius, Beast of Night Table of Contents

- [Nightreign Gladius, Beast of Night: About](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Gladius_Beast_of_Night#about)
- [Nightreign Gladius, Beast of Night: Information](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Gladius_Beast_of_Night#information)
- [Nightreign Gladius, Beast of Night: Guide](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Gladius_Beast_of_Night#guide)

### About Gladius, Beast of Night in ER Nightreign

- This is the nightlord encountered during the [Tricephalos](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Tricephalos "Tricephalos") expedition
- This boss must be defeated to unlock additional expeditions
- [Revenant's remembrance quest](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Revenant "Revenant") says that it requires defeating either [Fulghor](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Fulghor_Champion_of_Nightglow "Fulghor Champion of Nightglow") or Gladius, but as of app version 1.01.2, only Gladius will actually advance her quest
- This boss is featured in Nightreign's [Network Test](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Network_Test "Network Test")

### Combat information of Gladius, Beast of Night

#### Negations (or Absorptions)

The [negation](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Calculating_Damage "Calculating Damage") numbers are the % of your damage that gets blocked. For example, if a negation is 60, 40% of that damage by that type will go through and 60% will be negated. Bigger number = less damage. A negation of 100 means no damage goes through, and a negation of -100 mean the enemy takes 2x damage from that source. 0 means damage goes pretty much as is.

#### Resistances

### Elden Ring Nightreign Gladius Beast of Night Boss Guide

#### Gladius Beast of Night Boss Video Guide

[video coming soon]

#### Gladius Beast of Night Fight Strategy

**The Best Tips for Gladius Beast of Night:**

Gladius, Beast of Night (Tricephalos), is a three-headed wolf carrying a sword chained to its back. In its original form, its attacks and combo strings are fairly straightforward, making it easy enough for players to dodge and counterattack. Occasionally, it uses the chained sword to sweep across the battlefield, covering a wide area that can damage even players positioned behind it if the attack isn't dodged in time. Once its health drops to a certain point, though, Gladius splits into three separate wolves, with one of them still carrying the sword. At that point, a group of players can split up the three wolves' attention, allowing for one-on-one fights with each until the boss eventually reforms back into the Tricephalos.

##### Phase 1

In this opening phase, Gladius relies on basic swipes, slams, fire breath, and bites from its three jaws. Most of its attacks only reach a short distance, with the exception of when it drags its sword around the battlefield using the chain. Players tend to find this first form manageable, since its attacks are easy to dodge while sticking close to retaliate. Gladius is also extremely weak to Holy Damage, so it's worth planning a run around locations that offer gear or upgrades dealing that damage type.

As mentioned, Gladius occasionally uses its chained sword for wide sweeping attacks or slams, swinging both the sword and the chain itself across the battlefield. Even players positioned behind Gladius need to stay cautious during these sweeps, since they can still take damage even while attacking from that angle. Despite this, the fight remains fairly simple overall, since dodging toward the chain or sword is usually enough to avoid these attacks entirely. Successfully dodging gives players a window to land one or two attacks before Gladius recovers and resumes its assault.

##### Phase 2

Once Gladius's health reaches 75%, it becomes wrapped in flames and turns into a fireball that flies forward before materializing again, this time splitting into three separate wolves with their own basic attack strings. These three wolves alternate between passive and aggressive states, so players can focus their attention on whichever wolf is currently being aggressive. The wolf carrying the sword acts as the pack leader and will occasionally command the other two to attack at the same time, which can quickly overwhelm an unprepared solo player. Because a lone player can be punished heavily by this pack, it's generally recommended that solo players retreat from the wolves until they merge back into the Tricephalos. Groups, on the other hand, have the option of luring the wolves apart to fight them individually, and certain ultimate abilities, such as those belonging to Guardian and Raider, are particularly effective against the pack.

After roughly 45 seconds, the three wolves reform back into Gladius. This time, however, Gladius returns with stronger variants of its attacks combined with fire. Whenever it attacks with its sword, there's now a chance it performs the Sword Slam Blast, soaring into the air before diving down and striking the ground with its sword to create an explosion. Gladius can also drive its burning sword into the ground and pull it back out to send a wave of fire forward. Generally speaking, players want to stay close to Gladius's side as much as possible during this phase, since most of its attacks are aimed forward. Occasionally, though, the Tricephalos channels a spell that creates a blast around itself, though this is easy to evade thanks to its small area of effect.

When **Gladius** is defeated for the first time, players will unlock six new [Expeditions](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Expeditions "Expeditions"). They will also receive the [Night of the Beast](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Night_of_The_Beast "Night of The Beast") and [Old Pocketwatch](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Old_Pocketwatch "Old Pocketwatch") relics, giving players the following effects once equipped:

- [Night of the Beast](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Night_of_The_Beast "Night of The Beast")
  - Stamina recovers with each successful attack +1
  - Starting armament deals fire damage
- [Old Pocketwatch](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Old_Pocketwatch "Old Pocketwatch")
  - [FP](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Fp "Fp") Restoration upon Successive Attacks
  - [Dexterity](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Dexterity "Dexterity") +3

### Elden Ring Nightreign Gladius, Beast of Night (Everdark Sovereign) Boss Guide

#### Gladius, Beast of Night (Everdark Sovereign) Video Guide

[video coming soon]

#### Gladius, Beast of Night (Everdark Sovereign) Fight Strategy

#### Everdark Gladius Overview

Initially, **Everdark Gladius** will start fighting as three hounds, with one wielding a blade, similar to the base **Gladius** fight. During this form, the hounds will slowly walk up to the player, with the sword-wielding hound trailing the two hounds. It will use normal hound attacks to swarm at the [Nightfarer](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Nightfarers "Nightfarers") if playing solo, overwhelming them. During this phase, the player should look into luring one hound at a time, as its attacks can easily be dodged, allowing for retaliation. Its basic attacks will mostly consist of different variants of bite, such as a normal bite as it runs at the player, or it can use two consecutive bites that can catch impatient players.

Once its health reaches around 70%, **Everdark Gladius** will merge to become the Tricephalos, gaining attacks significantly stronger than when it was separated. When merged into one, **Everdark Gladius** can use lethal attacks that can generate blasts or quickly pounce at the player from afar. It will also utilize its sword to slash at the player or create flaming fissures all over the arena.

Eventually, **Everdark Gladius** will separate into three again, this time, adding more attacks to its repertoire. In the third phase, **Everdark Gladius** can spew fire from its sword, spreading across the area in front of where it swipes. After a short while, it will merge back again into the Tricephalos. **Everdark Gladius** can be difficult to catch in this phase, as it will be highly mobile with attacks that can keep the player away from it. However, once players get to be in melee distance of **Everdark Gladius**, they can avoid the chains and the sword that hits mid-range, allowing players to retaliate as it misses its attacks.

**Everdark Gladius** will still be weak against [![holy upgrade affinity elden ring wiki guide 60px](https://static0.fextralifeimages.com/file/eldenringnightreign/thumb/2/23/Holy-upgrade-affinity-elden-ring-nightreign-wiki-guide-85px.png/20px-Holy-upgrade-affinity-elden-ring-nightreign-wiki-guide-85px.png)](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Holy_Damage "Holy Damage") [Holy](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Holy_Damage "Holy Damage"), so it is recommended for players to plan their route to obtain [Incantations](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Incantations "Incantations") and [Weapons](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Weapons "Weapons") that deal Holy damage. However, if players cannot find any gear related to [![holy upgrade affinity elden ring wiki guide 60px](https://static0.fextralifeimages.com/file/eldenringnightreign/thumb/2/23/Holy-upgrade-affinity-elden-ring-nightreign-wiki-guide-85px.png/20px-Holy-upgrade-affinity-elden-ring-nightreign-wiki-guide-85px.png)](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Holy_Damage "Holy Damage") [Holy](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Holy_Damage "Holy Damage"), **Everdark Gladius** is a bit susceptible to the [Sleep](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Sleep "Sleep") status effect, so players can find it effective if they can build it up on the boss.

#### Phase 1

The fight with **Everdark Gladius** will start against the three hounds, identical to what the players faced during the base Gladius fight. In this form, the three hounds will attack the player separately with basic attacks that can be easily dodged. However, players shouldn't underestimate this form, as the hounds can easily overwhelm players when they attack as a group. Players should lure the hounds one at a time to open them up to attacks. The sword-wielding hound will be trailing the other two hounds, so players can avoid the encounter with it and focus on the two hounds instead, as it will have attacks that are more difficult to deal with. Players should also be attentive to the position of the hounds during this phase, keeping them on the screen to avoid being backstabbed or *hounded*. When players focus on only one hound, it can easily be staggered, allowing players to deal more damage to it instead of spreading the stagger build-up on all hounds.

#### Phase 2

When **Everdark Gladius'**s health reaches around 70%, it will merge into the **Tricephalos**. For all encounters with **Everdark Gladius**, it will always do its opening attack, wherein it will bite on the sword and perform two dash attacks (**Slice and Dice**) at the player. Players can dodge roll towards **Everdark Gladius** to avoid taking damage. In **Phase 2**, **Everdark Gladius** will be more mobile, performing lunging attacks and combining them with its sword that can hit from afar. It can also perform a new attack, wherein it will launch its sword towards the sky, imbue it with fire, then slam it on the ground, generating an explosion that covers a lot of ground in the arena. This move is heavily telegraphed, as the **Everdark Gladius** will always perform this move after slashing its sword on the ground twice. When **Everdark Gladius** launches its sword up, players should sprint away from it as far as possible to be able to dodge it more easily or to escape its blast radius. During Phase 2, players should be patiently waiting for their turn to attack, as **Everdark Gladius** will have zoning attacks that can make it difficult for players to approach it.

#### Phase 3

**Everdark Gladius** will then split into three again after its health reaches around 30%-40%, with the hounds becoming more aggressive and having additional attacks. At the start of the third phase, right after **Everdark Gladius** splits, the hounds will then perform **Flaming Dashes** towards the player. Players will have to know the location of each hound, then strafe sideways or dodge roll the dashes at the moment of impact to avoid taking damage. Then, it will continue using then attacks during the first phase. However, the sword-wielding hound can send out flames (**Desecrated Ground**) toward the player's direction, so players staying away from it can be damaged.

After a short while, the three hounds will transform back into its **Tricephalos** form, which is an easier form to fight against compared to the three hounds. In this form, players should always stick beside **Everdark Gladius** to avoid getting hit by the chain and the sword from mid-range while also being able to retaliate against it when possible. Once **Everdark Gladius** is defeated, players can purchase the [Dark Night of the Beast](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Dark_Night_of_The_Beast "Dark Night of The Beast") from [Collector Signboard](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Collector_Signboard "Collector Signboard").

After the **Sword Slashes**, **Everdark Gladius** will usually follow up with the **Flaming Sword Slam**. | When **Everdark Gladius** slashes its sword onto the ground, players should run away from it to avoid the follow-up attack. |
| Flaming Sword Slam | **Everdark Gladius** throws its sword at the sky, imbuing it with fire. **Everdark Gladius** will then slam it onto the ground, generating a large explosion with flaming fissures on the ground. | If players are inside the blast radius of the **Flaming Sword Slam**, they can dodge roll exactly as the explosion occurs to avoid being damaged. |

For the last hit, **Everdark Gladius** will pounce towards the player's direction. | When **Everdark Gladius** imbues its jaws with fire, players should move away from it or stick to its rear. |
| Sword Sweep | **Everdark Gladius** sweeps its sword around it twice, generating weak flames around the circle. | Players can dodge roll towards the sword's chain as it hits them to avoid taking damage. |

Then, as each hound dashes toward the player, they can strafe or dodge roll sideways to avoid getting hit by the wolves. |
| Desecrated Ground | The hound carrying the sword spins and conjures fire that spreads on the ground, directed at the player. **Everdark Gladius** will also do this once it merges back into the **Tricephalos** for the final time. | Players can move away from the hound with the sword once it spins. When it sends out fire, there will be small safe spots on it that players can stand on to avoid getting hit. |
| Upward Bite | A hound bites at the player, then does a follow-up upward bite for its finisher. | Players can dodge roll away from the first bite to gain distance, then move and dodge roll to the right as the hound goes for the second bite. |

# Adel Baron of Night

**Adel, Baron of Night**, also known as **Gaping Jaw**, is a **[Nightlord Boss](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Bosses "Bosses")** in **[Nightreign](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Elden_Ring_Nightreign_Wiki "Elden Ring Nightreign Wiki")**. Encountered at the end of the [Gaping Jaw](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Gaping_Jaw "Gaping Jaw") Expedition, **Adel** is fought on the third and final day. This page covers important details about **Adel, Baron of Night**, such as the Gaping Jaw's weaknesses, attacks, rewards, and the best strategies for defeating this powerful Nightlord.

- [Click here for the Everdark Sovereign variant of Adel, Baron of Night.](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Adel_Baron_of_Night_Everdark_Sovereign_(gaping_Jaw) "Adel Baron of Night Everdark Sovereign (gaping Jaw)")

> A colossal, crooked black frame capable of harboring lightning, with massive jaws, lined with grinding teeth to devour anything and everything it encounters.
>
> Only poison will stop it in its tracks.

### Elden Ring Nightreign Adel, Baron of Night Boss

- This is the Nightlord encountered during the [Gaping Jaw](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Gaping_Jaw "Gaping Jaw") expedition
- The Everdark Sovereign version of the Gaping Jaw expedition has different boss mechanics.

### Adel, Baron of Night Combat Information

### Elden Ring Nightreign Adel, Baron of Night Boss Guide

#### Adel, Baron of Night Fight Strategy

**The Best Tips for Adel, Baron of Night:**

**Adel, Baron of Night** **(**[Gaping Jaw](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Gaping_Jaw "Gaping Jaw")**)** is a massive black dragon with a large snout lined with gnarled teeth to grab onto its enemies. In the first part of the fight, **Adel** will often use its snout and its large frame to attack players, crushing those who are stubborn enough to get in its path. **Adel** will erratically rampage through the battlefield, making it hard for players to catch up to it.

Once **Adel's' *health reaches a certain threshold, it will throw a tantrum, fully utilizing the Lightning kept within its body.*** *Adel''***s** basic attacks will be infused with Lightning, creating wide explosions and adding Lightning properties to their physical attacks. Players are generally suggested to stay underneath or beside **Adel**, avoiding the direction of its jaws.

##### Phase 1

In Phase 1, **Adel''***s'* attacks will be straightforward, such as using its snout to grab players, its claws to swipe at players, or its body frame to tackle or charge towards players. The attack that players must be really cautious of is the **Lightning Rush**, which is when **Adel** opens its jaw widely and charges forward, with caught players being chewed and thrown by **Adel**, causing blood loss.

This attack can grab multiple players, so it is recommended to avoid staying too long in front of **Adel**, as it can potentially kill players, even with full health. When a player is grabbed, the party members should pile on **Adel** and constantly attack it to free the player caught by the [Gaping Jaw](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Gaping_Jaw "Gaping Jaw").

As stated earlier, **Adel** is extremely weak to [Poison](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Poison "Poison"), as it will slow the boss down when inflicted. When **Adel** is poisoned, it will pause and expel the poison from its body through its mouth, allowing players to attack. Also, during this phase, **Adel's** range is extremely limited.

When players are having a difficult time and need to reset, they can sprint away from **Adel** to safety to heal or apply buffs. Players with low health can move out of the battle and heal as their allies continue fighting the [Nightlord](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Bosses "Bosses").

##### Phase 2

When **Adel's** [HP](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Hp "Hp") drops to 50%, it will channel a lightning surge that spreads across the battlefield. Players can dodge this by sprinting away from the boss, or dodge rolling at the moment of impact. **Adel** will then launch itself into the air, then crash down onto the ground, damaging players near the impact zone. **Adel** may occasionally repeat this attack string, so players need to be aware of how to evade this.

**Adel** will then have minor changes to its appearance, with purple Lightning flowing in its body. In this phase, **Adel's** attacks will be infused with [Lightning damage](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Lightning_Damage "Lightning Damage"), and it will become more resistant to [Status Effects](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Status_Effects "Status Effects"). Some attacks, such as the Snout Slam, will generate fissures with electricity that will explode and damage players in an AoE.

When evading these attacks, players must roll towards **Adel** to retaliate against the boss while also dodging most of the attacks. Also, even if **Adel** is more resistant to [Poison](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Poison "Poison") in this phase, players are still recommended to keep inflicting **Adel** with it to slow it down and create a brief opening to attack.

Due to **Adel** having more attack strings in its arsenal and increased resistances, the latter phase will be slower and more difficult than the first. As **Adel** gains range with its [Lightning](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Lightning_Damage "Lightning Damage") attacks, ranged [Nightfarers](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Nightfarers "Nightfarers") or players with low health should be more cautious when disengaging to heal and reset, as there could be stray fissures or Lightning that can knock them out.

#### Gaping Jaw Everdark Sovereign Strategy

In the Everdark Sovereign version of Adel, Baron of Night, the boss gains new and more dangerous attacks. Note that it starts in phase 2 of the original Adel, Baron of Night fight, so any poison infliction no longer causes it to stumble and vomit. It immediately opens the fight with a Lightning Snout Slam, so avoid blindly charging in and jump over the fissures before moving in to attack.

The first new move is Lightning Teleport. Adel starts by rising slightly into the air while building up purple energy around his body. After a brief charge, he suddenly teleports four times through the sky, each jump leaving behind a trail of purple lightning that lingers for a moment.

Try to keep your camera on him and move constantly, dodging sideways between each flash of light to avoid being caught. After the fourth teleport, he stops and appears close to bite you.

Watch for his body to reappear and roll the moment he lunges forward to avoid the bite. But the move doesn't end there. He vanishes again and teleports several more times, once again spreading lightning trails throughout the arena. The final part of the attack ends with Adel slamming his jaws into the ground, causing a strong shockwave.

If you time your dodge right as his jaws hit the ground, you can safely avoid the blast and quickly rush in. He stays still for a short moment after this final slam, which gives you a safe window to land one or two melee hits before he recovers.

The other new attack is called Snout Slam AOE. Adel lifts his head high and begins glowing with dark purple energy, holding that pose for a second or two. This is your warning to get ready. He then slams his snout into the ground with heavy force, causing parts of the ground to break and shake while sending out a burst of energy around him.

The area of effect can knock you back if you're too close, so back away or time your roll right as the slam hits. After the impact, Adel doesn't move right away, especially if you're behind him, giving you a short chance to sneak in a heavy melee strike or a charged combo before he starts moving again.

Once you take it down to about 60-50% HP, Adel unleashes phase 3. Like with Lightning Teleport, Adel will hover off the battlefield and do several teleports in quick succession before unleashing a small burst of lightning damage with lingering lightning strikes.

Disengage lock-on and begin backing away once this happens. Once it finishes this part of the attack, it charges up again in a bright purple glow before making a large vertical leap off the battlefield.

The purple beam of light telegraphs where it will hit, and on impact it will discharge a lightning AOE that hits in a wide area and deals nearly lethal amounts of damage.

While this is happening, it will also generate a Great Tornado, tearing into the HP of any players caught in the winds. Spiritsprings will appear outside the tornado, and anyone staying outside will begin taking damage over time.

Thus, to fully avoid this attack, disengage lock-on, begin backing away, look for the purple beam once Adel has jumped off the battlefield, and sprint directly away so as not to get caught in the storm as it is forming. Then, when the spiritsprings appear, turn around and jump back into the tornado to continue the fight.

This move can be cancelled with any attack that staggers it, but strike it in the wind-up for the second part of the attack; otherwise you only cancel the lightning discharge and not the tornado.

Adel will continue fighting as normal, and there is nothing stopping Adel from diving in and out of the tornado. If it exits your reach, stay on the defensive and wait for it to come back. Watch out for its grabs in phase 3, because the full grab animation lasts long enough to trigger bleed on the victim twice in succession, which is lethal to anyone without extraordinary amounts of HP or bleed resistance.

If an ally gets grabbed, the only way to cancel it early is by staggering it with attacks like the Wylder's [Onslaught Stake](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Onslaught_Stake "Onslaught Stake") or a Raider's fully charged [Retaliate](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Retaliate "Retaliate").

A single strike from any weapon with an anti-dragon effect like [Dragonwound Grease](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Dragonwound_Grease "Dragonwound Grease") will also immediately cancel the grab animation and free the victim.

While the Great Tornado is up, Adel will eventually prepare a Lightning Tantrum. The charging animation causes the tornado to dissipate, freeing up the rest of the battlefield and serving as the players' cue to back away again. However, it will immediately follow up with another Lightning Snout Slam; watch where it lands before resuming the assault.

#### Gnoster Wisdom of Night Boss Video Guide

#### Gnoster Wisdom of Night Fight Strategy

**The Best Tips for Gnoster Wisdom of Night:**

Gnoster Wisdom of Night, encountered during the [Sentient Pest](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Sentient_Pest "Sentient Pest") expedition,is a [Nightlord](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Bosses "Bosses") consisting of two separate enemies, Faurtis and Gnoster. Faurtis takes the form of a large, scorpion-like creature whose attacks, things like pincer strikes, slams, and lunges, are clearly telegraphed, giving players time to react appropriately. Gnoster, on the other hand, spends most of the fight flying, which makes it a particularly awkward target for melee-focused Nightfarers trying to land hits. Throughout the encounter, Gnoster fires magical projectiles directly at players, and these can be avoided either by rolling through them or simply running clear. Despite being two separate creatures, Faurtis and Gnoster share a single collective health bar, meaning damage dealt to either one chips away at the same overall HP pool. Because of this, players are encouraged to bring [Weapons](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Weapons "Weapons") or [Incantations](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Incantations "Incantations") that deal [![fire upgrade affinity elden ring nightreign wiki guide 25px](https://static0.fextralifeimages.com/file/eldenringnightreign/8/8f/Fire-upgrade-affinity-elden-ring-nightreign-wiki-guide-25px.png)](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Fire_Damage "Fire Damage") [Fire](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Fire_Damage "Fire Damage") damage, since this is especially effective against Gnoster.

##### Phase 1

In this first phase, both Gnoster and Faurtis rely on fairly simple attacks that can be handled with properly timed rolls. The Moth, referring to Gnoster, mainly uses two attacks during this stage. One involves firing six magical projectiles at players two at a time, requiring players to strafe sideways while dodging them. The other is a quick burst of mist that applies a debuff, a parasite that deals damage and slows down anyone caught inside it, though this can be removed by having another player attack the affected ally. The Moth can also make the sky shimmer as it fires projectiles upward, which are then followed shortly after by a rain of projectiles falling in a cone shape, showering the area below with volleys of light. When this particular attack triggers, staying directly underneath the Moth is actually the safest place to be.

Meanwhile, Faurtis, referred to here as the Shears, attacks using its legs and pincers. If a player is positioned to its side, it can stomp the ground on that same side, causing spikes to burst out of the earth in front of where it struck. It also has lunging claw attacks that can catch players off guard due to their unexpectedly quick speed. Every so often, the Shears encases itself in a white shell that significantly reduces incoming damage, and when this happens, it's a good cue for players to shift focus toward the flying Moth instead. Since the Moth is difficult to hit while airborne, having at least one [Ironeye](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Ironeye "Ironeye") in the group is recommended to keep dealing damage to it during these stretches.

##### Phase 2

Once Gnoster's health drops to 50%, the Moth lands on top of the Shears' head and remains there for the rest of the fight. From this point on, the two creatures combine their attacks, with the Moth launching dangerous projectiles while the Shears uses its body to strike directly. These attacks often happen at the same time, such as the Shears charging at a player while the Moth simultaneously fires off its projectiles.

The Moth also picks up a new attack in this phase: an orbital beam that tracks the player after it emits a burst of light. When this attack begins, the safest approach is to play defensively and keep moving around the battlefield, since the beam can hit repeatedly once it makes contact. This phase is considerably tougher than the first, so a more defensive approach against the Sentient Pest is recommended overall. When the Shears performs one of its slower physical attacks, players can stay close to its side and counterattack safely. Generally, positioning on the sides of Gnoster helps players avoid both its charging attacks and the Moth's projectiles before they even happen.

#### Gnoster Wisdom of Night Everdark Sovereign (Sentient Pest) Fight Strategy

The **Everdark Sovereign** variant of **Gnoster** plays out similarly to the regular version (Gnoster Wisdom of Night), with the **Everdark Sovereign Gnoster** starting in the second form of the regular version. In the first phase of the fight, **Gnoster** will be mounted on **Faurtis** (the Scorpion), using attacks that players have encountered in the regular fight. During this phase, players are recommended to stay on the side or rear of **Faurtis** to avoid taking damage, as most of its attacks will consist of charging forward and sending out a barrage of light projectiles to its chosen target. However, when **Gnoster'**s health is depleted, players will face three individual bosses simultaneously: **Animus, Ascendant Light**, **Gnoster, Wisdom of Night**, and **Faurtis Stoneshield**. In this phase, the three bosses will attack independently so that players grouped into three can draw out one boss each and fight them separately. An interesting mechanic in this fight is that when **Faurtis Stoneshield'**s health is depleted, the **Animus** will possess it, regaining its HP and enhancing its attacks.

##### Phase 1

At the beginning of the fight, **Everdark Sovereign Gnoster** will start in the second phase of the original fight. During this phase, **Everdark Sovereign Gnoster** will be directing light projectiles toward its chosen target, although players can easily react to the attacks by either positioning themselves underneath **Faurtis** or by moving away from its front to avoid the *Enhanced Charging Attack*. **Gnoster** can also channel an orbital strike, focused on one area, which can be easily avoided by the [Nightfarers](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Nightfarers "Nightfarers"), as the attack will be stationary. Due to the attacks being easily evaded, players can freely hit the boss until its health is depleted, which then transitions into **Phase 2**.

##### Phase 2

When **Everdark Sovereign Gnoster's** health is depleted, it will split into three bosses: **Animus, Ascendant Light**; **Gnoster, Wisdom of Night**; and **Faurtis Stoneshield**. In this phase, players can individually focus on their chosen boss to simplify the fight. **Gnoster** will begin using its *Poison Mist* attack, which inflicts multiple damage ticks while building up [![poison status effect elden ring wiki guide 25px](https://static0.fextralifeimages.com/file/eldenringnightreign/3/3a/Poison_status_effect_elden_ring_wiki_guide_25px.png)](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Poison "Poison") [Poison](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Poison "Poison") on those caught in the mist. It will also fire light projectiles that can be dodged by strafing or rolling sideways.

**Faurtis Stoneshield** retains the same attacks from the first phase of the regular variant (see Gnoster Wisdom of Night), including stomps that trigger spikes emerging from the ground. These close-range attacks are relatively simple, so it is recommended to defeat **Gnoster** first before focusing on **Faurtis** **Stoneshield** to make the fight more manageable.

Once **Faurtis Stoneshield's** health is depleted, **Animus, Ascendant Light** will possess it, making **Faurtis** more aggressive and enhancing its attacks. In this state, **Faurtis** gains lunging and charge attacks aimed at its target's position. Players should avoid standing in front of **Faurtis** for extended periods of time to minimize risk. Occasionally, when possessed, **Faurtis** will roar, signaling the start of its *Tantrum* attack, where it repeatedly slams its pincers into the ground, creating explosive fissures. During this sequence, its erratic behavior can make it difficult for players to dodge if they stick close to the boss, so it is recommended to sprint away as it finishes the attack.

**Animus**will continue to possess **Faurtis Stoneshield** whenever its health drops. To fully defeat this **Everdark Sovereign** variant of **Gnoster Wisdom of Night**, players must also deplete **Animus, Ascendant Light's** health.

#### Elden Ring Nightreign Gnoster Wisdom of Night Everdark Sovereign (Sentient Pest) Lore, Notes & Other Trivia

- Like all Nightlords, the bosses' names have a meaning in a real-life language:
  - *Animus* is a Latin word for *soul*, fitting how Animus rises from the corpse of Gnoster. In addition, it can "possess" Faurtis upon its death, much like a "soul" re-inhabiting a body.
  - *Gnoster* is most likely a merge of *Gnosis* (Greek for *knowledge*) and *noster* (Latin for *our*), fitting the multi-enemy nature of the encounter, and Gnoster's use of magic attacks - an element defined by knowledge.
  - *Faurtis* is likely derived from the Latin word *Fortis*, meaning *brave* or *strong*, fitting the Stoneshield's powerful physical attacks.

Encountered at the end of the [Augur](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Augur "Augur") Expedition, Maris is an aquatic foe whose body is primarily composed of water, utilizing powerful ranged attacks, area-of-effect (AoE) abilities, and unique combat mechanics. This page covers information regarding **Maris, Fathom of Night's** weaknesses, attacks, rewards, drops, and optimal strategies for defeating this Nightlord.

#### Negations (or Absorptions)

The [negation](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Calculating_Damage "Calculating Damage") numbers are the % of your damage that gets blocked. For example, if a negation is 60, 40% of that damage by that type will go through and 60% will be negated. Bigger number = less damage. A negation of 100 means no damage goes through, and a negation of -100 mean the enemy takes 2x damage from that source. 0 means damage goes pretty much as is.

#### Resistances

The resistance numbers are the buildup amount to trigger it. For example, if a resistance is 100 you must deal 100 points of the given buildup to trigger it. Note that these go down over time, and increase each time the effect procs. The values after the "/"s indicate the increased resistances after each successive proc.

### Elden Ring Nightreign Maris Fathom of Night Boss Guide

#### Augur Boss Fight Strategy

**Maris, Fathom of Night ([Augur](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Augur "Augur")'***) **is a squid-like boss that floats gently through the air, although it can hover near the ground occasionally, allowing melee-based [Nightfarers](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Nightfarers "Nightfarers") to attack it momentarily.** Maris''***s** abilities and attacks revolve around water and wind elements, creating sweeping waves, gusts of wind, and aquatic summons such as explosive jellyfish.

This boss can also hypnotize players in a wide area, which can be devastating if it is fully channeled. **Maris** is highly vulnerable to [Lightning Damage](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Lightning_Damage "Lightning Damage"), so players should plan their builds accordingly before starting their run.

Throughout the fight, **Maris** will summon hazardous creatures around the battlefield, which are recommended to be attacked by the players. For example, the jellyfish-like bombs will slowly drift toward players, exploding on contact or after a short delay. These can be avoided, as players can outrun the slow movement of these creatures. However, players can also use ranged attacks on them when they are close to **Maris**, as they will deal damage to the boss when they explode.

**Maris** can also summon tentacles coming out of the ground, which will lash out at players around it. Players can walk away from these creatures, but it will be better if these tentacles are attacked, as they only take a few hits to be disposed of.

The attack that players have to be cautious of when fighting **Maris** is its **Hypnosis** attack, wherein it will have a distinct audio cue before flying and curling into a ball in the ground. It will then channel a spell that builds up the Sleep [Status Effect](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Status_Effects "Status Effects") on players.

When players are fully afflicted with [Sleep](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Sleep "Sleep"), players will be dealt damage over time that will usually put them in a near-death state if a party member survives the attack. To counter this attack, players must charge towards **Maris** after hearing the audio cue for the attack, then attack it until it stops channeling the spell. Using attacks or [Incantations](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Incantations "Incantations") that deal [Lightning damage](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Lightning_Damage "Lightning Damage") will be more effective, as it will stop the spell much faster.

**Maris** uses a range of elemental abilities, such as summoning waves of water, launching gusts of wind, or violently whipping its body to create a damaging shockwave. It can also cause water to appear from beneath the ground, damaging players caught in its vicinity.

These attacks will often leave **Maris** exposed, as it will either be idle or take a long time to recover, giving players a substantial amount of time to counterattack. Dodging effectively and staying mobile will create opportunities for players to attack.

Once **Maris** drops to around 50% health, it will become more aggressive. It will begin flying higher and launching more attacks, such as summoning additional jellyfish creatures, and unleashing large, luminous droplets of water that explode once it reaches the ground.

Players should avoid these droplets by sprinting away to escape the blast radius. Although the second phase is more chaotic, most of **Maris's** attacks will still be telegraphed, allowing players to retaliate or dodge in time.

### Elden Ring Nightreign Fulghor Maris Fathom of Night Everdark Sovereign (Augur) Boss Guide

#### Maris Fathom of Night Everdark Sovereign (Augur) Fight Strategy

The **Everdark Sovereign** variant of **Maris** will have significant changes compared to the regular encounter (see Maris Fathom of Night), increasing the difficulty of the boss.

Similar to the **Everdark Sovereign** variants of other [bosses](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Bosses "Bosses"), such as [Fulghor](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Fulghor_Champion_of_Nightglow_Everdark_Sovereign_(darkdrift_Knight) "Fulghor Champion of Nightglow Everdark Sovereign (darkdrift Knight)"), the fight with **Maris** is expected to start during the second phase of the fight, wherein **Augur** will launch more aggressive attacks. Additionally, **Everdark Sovereign Maris** will be summoning more jellyfish in the arena, making it difficult for players to navigate around as they chase the flying **Augur** around the battlefield.

**Everdark Sovereign Maris** will still have the same weakness as its regular variant, which is [![lightning upgrade affinity elden ring wiki guide 60px](https://static0.fextralifeimages.com/file/eldenringnightreign/thumb/5/57/Lightning-icon-elden-ring-nightreign-wiki-guide.png/20px-Lightning-icon-elden-ring-nightreign-wiki-guide.png)](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Lightning_Damage "Lightning Damage") [Lightning](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Lightning_Damage "Lightning Damage"). Players are recommended to plan routes that will yield Lightning [weapons](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Weapons "Weapons"), which will be of significant help for staggering **Everdark Sovereign Maris** whenever it starts channeling the **Hypnosis** attack.

After completing the 1st phase of the fight, **Maris Fathom of the Night** will drop a legendary **Storm Ruler.** From Software veterans will recognize this as a long line of flying bosses that have appeared in games such as Demon's Souls. Here are some tips and important mechanics Storm Ruler:

- Each player gets one - and you should use it. The **Storm Ruler** skill from the weapon is key to this fight.
- When you hold the skill, not attacking, just in the stance - **YOU REGAIN FP.** This is crucial since many players are reporting that they run out of FP during the fight, or believe that they have to play heavy-FP [Classes](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Classes "Classes") like [Recluse](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Recluse "Recluse") or [Revenant](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Revenant "Revenant")
- On the other hand, when you hold the skill without attacking for several seconds, you charge up a much stronger and larger attack. It creates a MASSIVE vertical attack.

**DON'T** spam the weapon art immediately, it will drain your FP in a few seconds.

The first phase against **Augur** is pretty straightforward and does not pose much of a challenge. It can be defeated quite easily if you know what you are doing. This first phase ends once players have depleted Maris Fathom of the Night first health bar. As it dies, it will leave a legendary weapon that, as previously mentioned, is **VERY IMPORTANT** for this fight. Note that all players will be able to loot this legendary weapon.

After a few short seconds, **Maris, Fathom of the Night** will emerge from the skies and enter the battlefield. In a way, it is a similar fight that the Elden Beast in base Elden Ring. Maris will fly across the sky and meteors will shoot from its body to the ground.

You will have to strike a balance in order to fight it using the legendary weapon, while also dodging the projectiles since attacking leaves you stuck to the ground for a few seconds. (specially if you fully charge the attack). Try to be on the move while you are not attacking in order to dodge incoming attacks.

As you remove almost half its health, Maris will enter its third phase, becoming an even bigger being, and meteors will float around its "Head" during the rest of the fight. During this phase it will also become more nimble, and agile, reaching higher speeds than in the previous ones.

Try to shoot the collar of meteors floating around it. You can lock onto each of them and use the legendary weapon art to destroy them. This meteor collar, allows Maris to shoot multiple targets at the same time, so dealing damage to them as fast as possible should be priority.

Once all of them are destroyed, Maris will fall down to the ground, stunned. Land as many hits as possible during this time.

Try to focus on the meteors ASAP to avoid multiple attacks. and repeat this process until **Maris Fathom of Night** is down. This fight is about endurance and can become quite long given the boss flying around the whole battlefield.

# Libra Creature of Night

'*Libra, Creature of Night**, also known as** Equilibrious Beast**, is a** [Nightlord Boss](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Bosses "Bosses") **in** [Nightreign](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Elden_Ring_Nightreign_Wiki "Elden Ring Nightreign Wiki")**. Encountered at the end of the [Equilibrious Beast](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Equilibrious_Beast "Equilibrious Beast") expedition,** Libra **is fought on the third and final day. This** Libra, Creature of Night **boss guide covers** Libra''***s** attacks, weaknesses, rewards, and strategies for defeating this Nightlord.

- [Click here for the Everdark Sovereign variant of Libra Creature of Night](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Libra_Creature_of_Night_Everdark_Sovereign_(equilibrious_Beast) "Libra Creature of Night Everdark Sovereign (equilibrious Beast)")

> A goat-headed being who pretends to be a man, said to be able to use a dubious form of alchemy. Counterfeit gold causes loss of sanity, beckoning madness. However, those who foment madness are sure to succumb to the selfsame malady in the end.

### Elden Ring Nightreign Libra, Creature of Night Boss

- This is the nightlord encountered during the [Equilibrious Beast](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Equilibrious_Beast "Equilibrious Beast") expedition
- Before the fight with **Libra**, players must interact with the [Scale-bearing Merchant](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Scale-bearing_Merchant "Scale-bearing Merchant"). This merchant can provide players with a random pool of buffs in exchange for a negative effect. Players may either take a deal or refuse it, and then the merchant will turn into **Libra**. Listed below are some of the possible choices that the **Scale-bearing Merchant** can give players:

-   - *I wish to have great strength* - Raises [Strength](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Strength "Strength") in exchange for all other stats
  - *I wish to have great dexterity* - Raises [Dexterity](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Dexterity "Dexterity") in exchange for all other stats
  - *I wish to expand my intellect* - Raises [Intelligence](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Intelligence "Intelligence") in exchange for all other stats
  - *I wish to have deep faith* - Raises [Faith](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Faith "Faith") in exchange for all other stats
  - *I wish to be in touch with the arcane* - Raises [Arcane](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Arcane "Arcane") in exchange for all other stats
  - *I want resistance to ailments* - Increases Resistances by +150, but lose 10% Stamina
  - *I want to hold death at bay* - Lose 20% max HP. When HP drops to 20% or lower, immediately heal back to 100% HP, once per battle. Does not trigger against damage that instantly kills you from above 20% HP.
  - *I desire a flask* - Adds a Flask Charge but lose 10% max HP

-   - *I desire a powerful weapon* - Lose 2 levels but randomly get one of the following: [Vyke's War Spear](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Vyke%27s_War_Spear "Vyke's War Spear"), [Black Knife](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Black_Knife "Black Knife"), [Erdtree Bow](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Erdtree_Bow "Erdtree Bow"), [Frenzied Flame Seal](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Frenzied_Flame_Seal "Frenzied Flame Seal"), [Fingerprint Stone Shield](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Fingerprint_Stone_Shield "Fingerprint Stone Shield"), [Miquellan Knight's Sword](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Miquellan_Knight%27s_Sword "Miquellan Knight's Sword"), [Ordovis's Greatsword](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Ordovis%27s_Greatsword "Ordovis's Greatsword"), [Halo Scythe](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Halo_Scythe "Halo Scythe"). Passive effects are determined randomly.
  - *I want to gain many levels* - Gain 3 levels but lose 1 every time you drink from your Flask
  - *I wish for eventual greatness* - Take a -30% HP, FP, and Stamina debuff for 120 seconds. After that debuff expires, gain a +20% HP, FP, and Stamina buff permanently. These effects are void the moment you are brought near-death.
  - *I want the power of a demon* - Grants an Eye that intermittently shoots enemies for small amount of damage and Madness buildup, or occasionally grants you a 10% attack boost for 10 seconds. It builds up [Madness](https://eldenringnightreign.wiki.fextralife.com/Madness "Madness") whenever it appears.
  - *I wish to fight at full strength -* Starts the player with an +25% HP and +10% damage for 60 seconds, but Libra also starts the fight with his meditation buff active, on top of a +10% damage negation buff for 100 seconds.

- Players can attack Libra to force the fight to begin, terminating all ongoing dialogue for players that have not accepted his deals
- If a player starts dialogue with Libra, a countdown appears over its forehead, lasting a total of about 60 seconds (6 seconds per dot on the symbol). If the countdown reaches zero before all three players have confirmed their decision on its deals, it will start the fight.
